title: Global Archive Metadata Discovery
business: A national historical archive managing millions of digitized document records.
problem: Researchers struggle to locate specific documents because legacy relational databases cannot efficiently perform full-text searches across unstructured OCR transcripts while simultaneously filtering by complex metadata facets.
solution: Apache Solr provides a distributed search platform that indexes both structured metadata fields and unstructured text content, enabling high-speed retrieval and multi-dimensional faceting.
steps: Define a schema.xml or use Managed Schema to map document metadata fields and full-text OCR content fields.
Configure text analysis chains using tokenizers and filters to normalize OCR transcripts for accurate matching.
Ingest document records into Solr collections, ensuring distributed indexing across the cluster for reliability.
Implement query-time faceting on metadata fields like 'Century' or 'DocumentType' to allow users to refine search results dynamically.
Expose the Solr search API to the frontend application to enable real-time discovery.
outcome: Researchers can perform rapid, intuitive searches across massive document sets, filtering results by metadata categories while maintaining full-text relevance.
limitation: Solr requires significant memory for heap management and index caching; excessive faceting on high-cardinality fields can lead to increased memory pressure, which is monitored via the Solr Admin UI dashboard.

questions.question: In Global Archive Metadata Discovery, why is Apache Solr chosen over a standard relational database?
options: It provides superior full-text search and multi-dimensional faceting capabilities.
It is the only database that supports historical document storage.
It eliminates the need for any metadata schema definitions.
It is exclusively designed for geospatial data management.
questions.explanation: Solr is specifically designed to handle the combination of unstructured text and structured metadata, which is the core requirement for the archive.
questions.evidence: Apache Solr provides a distributed search platform that indexes both structured metadata fields and unstructured text content, enabling high-speed retrieval and multi-dimensional faceting.

questions.question: In Global Archive Metadata Discovery, what is a primary operational limitation to monitor?
options: The inability to perform distributed indexing.
The lack of support for text analysis chains.
Memory pressure caused by high-cardinality faceting.
The requirement to use only Docker for deployment.
questions.explanation: High-cardinality fields in facets consume significant memory, which is a known trade-off in Solr performance.
questions.evidence: excessive faceting on high-cardinality fields can lead to increased memory pressure, which is monitored via the Solr Admin UI dashboard.
